text: {"overall_winner":"B","qualities":[{"evidence":"clear pro position in the opening and closing","quality":"argument focus","description":"The essay stays centered on a clear supportive claim about automated cars and returns to that claim at the end."},{"evidence":"three-part progression from benefits to problems to future laws","quality":"organization","description":"The essay develops its ideas in a more coherent sequence that helps the reader follow the argument."},{"evidence":"mentions of legal limits, liability, and safety concerns","quality":"use of source evidence","description":"The essay brings in several relevant details from the article to support its position instead of relying on one or two scattered points."},{"evidence":"explains texting, boredom, and driver alertness","quality":"explanatory development","description":"The essay more often explains why the article’s facts matter, showing the consequences of driverless cars rather than just naming them."},{"evidence":"smoother transitions such as \"Although,\" \"Even though,\" and \"Another reason\"","quality":"sentence flow","description":"The writing has more connective language that helps the essay move from one idea to the next more smoothly."}]}
